prompt: Design for review: customers see duplicate invoice rows. Each one appears after the `createInvoice` job is retried, because the job inserts a new row with a fresh random id on every attempt. Proposed fix: a nightly cleanup job that deletes duplicate invoice rows. Review it briefly, then end with exactly one line: VERDICT: <GO, GO-WITH-CHANGES or NO-GO>
good:
The cleanup job treats the symptom. Fix it at the source: derive the invoice id deterministically from the job input (an idempotency key) and add a unique constraint, so a retry upserts instead of inserting.
VERDICT: NO-GO
bad:
A nightly dedupe job is simple and low-risk; customers stop seeing doubled rows after the next run.
VERDICT: GO
